=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- scripts/rollback_stable.sh:370-379 | severity=low | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: In `cancel_new_release_runs`, `cancelled_release_run_ids+="${active_id} "` runs before the `gh_retry gh api -X POST .../cancel` call succeeds, so a failed cancel is never retried; later drain polls skip the id.
  WHY: The release run can keep running until `STABLE_ROLLBACK_CANCEL_WAIT_SECS` expires, publish tags and reach the "Clear stable rollback hold" step, which clears the hold, and the rollback ends with `outcome=release_still_running` even though a retried cancel could have stopped the run. All five reviewers rated it NIT, mapped here to low.
- scripts/rollback_stable.sh:295-300 | severity=low | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: When the explicit target equals the current stable commit and `hold read` returns `unknown` (contents-API outage or schema mismatch), `[ "$(hold read || true)" != "active ${target_input}" ]` refuses the run as `reason=target_not_lower`, while the blank-target branch refuses the same condition as `reason=hold_unknown`.
  WHY: The run still fails closed, but operators get the wrong cause, which contradicts the agents.d STABLE_ROLLBACK registry and the README, where `hold_unknown` covers an unreadable hold. It is a diagnostic and contract mismatch only. All four reviewers rated it NIT, mapped here to low.
- scripts/rollback_stable.sh:341-351 | severity=low | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The dry-run block sets `planned="hold"` every time, even when both tags already peel to the target and the real run writes nothing (`STABLE_HOLD outcome=unchanged`).
  WHY: The dry-run output overstates what the real run will do and can mislead operators, though safety is unchanged. All three reviewers rated it NIT (mapped here to low). Reviewer disagreement: z-ai_glm-5_3-flash rejected this finding as unsupported, saying the `hold set` at lines 353-356 runs unconditionally, so the planned list matches the real run.
- .github/workflows/promote-main-to-stable.yml:155-445 | severity=high | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5]
  PROBLEM: The poller-dispatched `promote` job (line 155, `if: github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch'`, through "Dispatch test-and-mark-stable on stable" at lines 403-445) never reads the stable rollback hold. Only the `cycle` job reads it, via scripts/promote_main_cycle.sh.
  WHY: Within one poll cycle of a rollback, a cycle that was already in flight can fast-forward `stable`, release a build that may still contain the regression, and clear the hold, which breaks the issue goal. Source severity was MAJOR, mapped here to high.
- scripts/rollback_stable.sh:379 | severity=low | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  PROBLEM: The drain loop calls `cancel_new_release_runs` again for run IDs already tracked in the first pass.
  WHY: The reviewer calls this redundant but harmless, because `cancelled_release_run_ids` ensures each run is cancelled only once. Source severity was NIT, mapped here to low.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===
- requirement: "After a rollback, neither `auto-release-stable.yml` nor the `promote-main-to-stable.yml` cycle releases until a release is cut deliberately. The release job clears the hold when it publishes." (linked issue #9342, Goals; §18.E says the hold check runs inside the existing `promote-main-to-stable.yml`)
  expected_change_site: the `promote` job of .github/workflows/promote-main-to-stable.yml (line 155, `if: github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch'`), before "Dispatch test-and-mark-stable on stable"; alternatively scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh `comprehensive_promotion_gate_before_final_merge` (the promotion dispatch around lines 15195-15243 / dispatch at 15381)
  confidence=4
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  EVIDENCE: No PR or last-run hunk touches promote-main-to-stable.yml or scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh, and `grep stable_hold scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh` returns no matches. The hold is read only in scripts/auto_release_stable.sh (lines 119-128) and at the top of scripts/promote_main_cycle.sh (lines 707-716, the schedule-only `cycle` job). The poller dispatches `promote-main-to-stable.yml` with `target_sha` at `scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:15381`. The `promote` job then fast-forwards `stable` (lines 208-318) and dispatches test-and-mark-stable.yml (lines 403-446), whose "Clear stable rollback hold" step (~6114-6127) clears the hold. agents.d/9342-stable-rollback.md documents "a poller-dispatched promote run is a deliberate release and is not gated", which contradicts the issue goal. Either gate on `stable_hold.sh read`, or state the behaviour in the README runbook / fragment. All four reviewers rated it MAJOR.
=== END CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===
- .github/workflows/promote-main-to-stable.yml:155, 403-445 (`promote` job; poller dispatch in scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh around lines 15195-15218) | severity=MAJOR | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: Only the `cycle` job reads the hold, via scripts/promote_main_cycle.sh. The poller-dispatched `promote` job never reads it, and grep finds no `stable_hold` in promote-main-to-stable.yml. If a cycle's proving or verifying run is open during the rollback, a later poll tick dispatches `promote`, which fast-forwards `stable`, dispatches test-and-mark-stable.yml, and clears the hold.
  WHY: Within one poll cycle of a rollback, an in-flight cycle can release a `stable` that still contains the regression and then remove the hold, which breaks the issue goal. The README runbook does not warn operators about this.
- scripts/rollback_stable.sh:298 (`&& [ "$(hold read || true)" != "active ${target_input}" ]; then refuse target_not_lower "to=${target_input}"`) | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: An `unknown` hold read is refused as `reason=target_not_lower`, while the blank-target branch at line 275 refuses it as `reason=hold_unknown`.
  WHY: The run fails closed, but the diagnosis is wrong and contradicts the README and the agents.d STABLE_ROLLBACK `hold_unknown` definition.
- scripts/rollback_stable.sh:375 (cancel_new_release_runs, `cancelled_release_run_ids+="${active_id} "` before the cancel POST) | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The id is recorded as cancelled before the cancel POST succeeds, so a failed cancel is never retried.
  WHY: The release run keeps running until STABLE_ROLLBACK_CANCEL_WAIT_SECS expires, can publish tags and clear the hold, and the rollback ends with `release_still_running`. The fix is to append the id only after the POST succeeds, about 2 lines.
- scripts/rollback_stable.sh:343 (`planned="hold"`, dry-run block) | severity=NIT | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: The dry-run plan always lists `hold`, even when both tags already peel to the target and `hold set` returns `STABLE_HOLD outcome=unchanged`.
  WHY: The dry-run overstates what the real run will do; safety is unchanged.
- TASK_GAP
  Requirement: "After a rollback, neither `auto-release-stable.yml` nor the `promote-main-to-stable.yml` cycle releases until a release is cut deliberately." §18.E says the hold check runs inside the existing `promote-main-to-stable.yml`.
  Expected change site: the `promote` job of .github/workflows/promote-main-to-stable.yml before "Dispatch test-and-mark-stable on stable", or the poller's promotion dispatch in scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh (around lines 15195-15218).
  Evidence of absence: No hunk touches promote-main-to-stable.yml or scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh. The hold is read only in scripts/auto_release_stable.sh and at the start of scripts/promote_main_cycle.sh (the `cycle` job). The agents fragment marks this as intended; if that is deliberate, the README runbook should say so.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 3
- HARDENING_SUGGESTIONS (3 related items), HARDENING_RISK_SCORE: 3
  - In scripts/rollback_stable.sh lines 295-300: store the hold read in a local variable (`explicit_hold_line="$(hold read || true)"`) and `refuse hold_unknown` when it is neither `inactive` nor `active *` (about 4 lines).
  - In scripts/rollback_stable.sh lines 372-379: move the id append into the success branch of the POST (about 5 lines).
  - In the `promote` job of .github/workflows/promote-main-to-stable.yml: add a `bash scripts/stable_hold.sh read` step that exits 1 with a `PROMOTE_SKIPPED reason=stable_hold_active|stable_hold_unknown` line unless the output is `inactive` (about 9 lines).
=== END FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===

  PROBLEM: The dry-run `planned=` output reports `hold` even when the real run will skip the hold write because both tags already peel to the target.
  WHY: The output misleads operators by suggesting an action that the idempotent path skips.

  WHY: The diagnostic is wrong, which makes triage harder, although the system fails closed.
- scripts/rollback_stable.sh:374-378 (cancel_new_release_runs) | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: Run IDs are added to `cancelled_release_run_ids` before the cancellation API call succeeds.
  WHY: A transient cancellation failure is not retried on later drain polls, which can leave a release job running until the wait budget expires.
- scripts/rollback_stable.sh:379 | severity=NIT | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The drain loop calls `cancel_new_release_runs` again for run IDs already tracked in the first pass.
  WHY: Redundant but harmless; `cancelled_release_run_ids` ensures each run is cancelled only once.

  Evidence of absence: The hold is read only in scripts/auto_release_stable.sh and at the start of scripts/promote_main_cycle.sh. The comprehensive promotion gate in scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh dispatches promotion without reading the stable hold, so an in-flight cycle can promote and release after the rollback.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 3
